subject: Mathematics
name: Foundation Mathematics, Units 3 and 4
about: VCE, Number, money, data and measurement at work
syllabus: VCE Mathematics Study Design (from 2023), Foundation Mathematics Units 3 and 4

points.title: Rearranging formulas
points.brief: Making another variable the subject of a formula, such as finding hours from total pay.

points.title: Linear relations in context
points.brief: A rule such as cost = 50 + 0.3 × km has a fixed part and a part that grows at a steady rate.

points.title: Graphing linear relations
points.brief: Plotting a linear rule gives a straight line whose steepness is the rate and whose start is the fixed amount.

points.title: Break-even points
points.brief: Graphing or solving two linear rules together, such as cost and income, finds the break-even point where they are equal.

points.title: Direct and indirect variation
points.brief: In direct variation both amounts grow together, such as cost and kilograms. In indirect variation one falls as the other rises, such as speed and travel time.

points.title: Significant figures and rounding
points.brief: Rounding to a number of significant figures or decimal places to suit the job.

points.title: Quick estimates
points.brief: Leading-digit estimates, interval estimates and rounding up or down (ceiling and floor) give fast, sensible answers.

points.title: Percentage error
points.brief: The error as a percentage of the true value shows how far off an estimate or measurement is.

points.title: Planning data collection
points.brief: Deciding what data to collect, from whom, how and why, so it suits its purpose and audience.

points.title: Statistical claims
points.brief: Checking a claim means asking who collected the data, how and from how many, and spotting errors and misleading uses of statistics.

points.title: Tables and spreadsheets
points.brief: Building tables and spreadsheets to organise data, including tables that sort people by two categories.

points.title: Modern graph types
points.brief: Bubble charts, radar charts, heat maps, sunburst, Mekko and stacked area charts, and when each suits the data.

points.title: Comparing groups with statistics
points.brief: Comparing medians, means, percentiles and standard deviations of two groups, such as wages in two jobs.

points.title: Cumulative frequency and percentiles
points.brief: A running total of frequencies shows how many values fall below a point, and percentiles mark where a value sits.

points.title: Long-run data and relative frequency
points.brief: Relative frequencies from long-term data, such as climate or disease records, estimate how likely an event is.

points.title: Predicting from data
points.brief: Reading values within a data range (interpolation) is safer than predicting beyond it (extrapolation).

points.title: Investments and compound interest
points.brief: Interest added to the balance earns interest itself, so investments grow faster than with simple interest.

points.title: Loans and repayments
points.brief: The total paid on a loan is the repayment times the number of payments, and the interest is that less the amount borrowed.

points.title: Credit and debit
points.brief: Debit spends your own money. Credit cards and buy now pay later borrow it, and interest and late fees can cost far more than the price.

points.title: Debt consolidation
points.brief: Combining several debts into one loan can cut interest and payments, but may stretch the time and the total paid.

points.title: Comparing costs of owning and renting
points.brief: Weighing up buying against renting a car or house means comparing total costs over time, not just the price.

points.title: Personal and business tax
points.brief: Income tax scales, the Medicare levy, superannuation and council rates for people, and company tax for businesses.

points.title: GST, invoices and BAS
points.brief: Businesses add GST to invoices and report what they collected and paid on a business activity statement.

points.title: Comparing insurance
points.brief: Comparing premiums, excesses and cover across insurance policies to choose one.

points.title: Inflation and the cost of living
points.brief: When prices rise, the same income buys less, so a pay rise below inflation is a cut in real terms.

points.title: Financial risk
points.brief: Investments and loans carry risk, from a single job loss to a national recession, and spreading money reduces it.

points.title: Reading financial trends
points.brief: Data on the gender pay gap, careers, exchange rates, share prices and recessions shows how money changes over time.

points.title: Transformations and symmetry
points.brief: Moving, flipping, turning and resizing shapes, and spotting symmetry, in designs, plans and everyday objects.

points.title: Scale models and plans
points.brief: Enlarging or reducing two- and three-dimensional plans and models by a scale factor.

points.title: Derived and non-metric measures
points.brief: Speed, fuel use per 100 km, flow rates and measures still used in trades, such as inches, and converting between them.

points.title: Area and volume for jobs
points.brief: Working out perimeter, area, surface area and volume of compound shapes, such as paint, tiles or concrete needed, allowing for waste.

points.title: Tolerance, accuracy and precision
points.brief: Every measurement has an error. Tolerance is the error allowed, accuracy is closeness to the true value, and precision is how fine the measure is.
